module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Rational distance problem

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_square#Rational_distance_problem)
- [mathoverflow/418260](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/418260/)
asked by user [Yuan Yang](https://mathoverflow.net/users/177957/yuan-yang)
- D19 in [Unsolved Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0)
by *Richard K. Guy*
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace RationalDistanceProblem

open EuclideanGeometry

def UnitSquareCorners : Fin 4 → ℝ² :=
  ![!₂[0, 0], !₂[1, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[0, 1]]

/--
Does there exist a point in the plane at rational distance from all four vertices of the unit square?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 51]
theorem rational_distance_problem :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P : ℝ² , ∀ i, ¬ Irrational (dist P (UnitSquareCorners i)) := by
  sorry

end RationalDistanceProblem

sources_consulted: https://mathoverflow.net/questions/418260/ (question body and all comments, via api.stackexchange.com)

https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0 (book page) and its front-matter PDF https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/bfm:978-0-387-26677-0/1 (table of contents: 'D19. Rational distances from the corners of a square. 283')

T. G. Berry, Points at rational distance from the corners of a unit square, Ann. Sc. Norm. Sup. Pisa (4) 17 (1990) 505-529, http://www.numdam.org/item/ASNSP_1990_4_17_4_505_0/ (PDF; text of pp. 506-529)
review.notes:
No defects found. The single theorem `RationalDistanceProblem.rational_distance_problem` states the rational distance problem literally as the cited sources pose it.

Definitions and Lean checks, done in /workspace/review:
- `ℝ²` is the scoped notation `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`. `rfl` confirms this in the file's context, so `dist` is Euclidean. A sup-metric `Fin 2 → ℝ` would have made (0,0) a trivial witness.
- `!₂[x, y]` is `WithLp.toLp 2 ![x, y]`. `¬ Irrational x` means x is the image of some rational.
- Proved: the four corners are (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (0,1); the sides have length 1 and the diagonals √2.
- Proved: `(∃ P : ℝ², ∀ i, ¬ Irrational (dist P (UnitSquareCorners i)))` is equivalent to the classical coordinate form. That form says there are real x, y with √(x²+y²), √((x−1)²+y²), √((x−1)²+(y−1)²) and √(x²+(y−1)²) all rational.
- Proved: no vertex is a witness (the diagonal is √2), and neither is the centre (√2/2).
- There is no division, natural-number subtraction or junk value anywhere in the statement.

Answer slot and status:
- In the default `google.answer` mode, `answer(sorry)` at `Prop` elaborates to `True`. This is the repository's convention for open questions.
- The right-hand side is the positive existence statement, which matches "Does there exist…?". It is not a negated conjecture.
- The `research open` tag matches the sources. The current Wikipedia text reads "It is not known whether any point in the plane is a rational distance from all four vertices of the unit square", MO 418260 has no answers, and Berry says the four-distance problem is unsettled.

Scope of the point:
- Wikipedia, its list of unsolved problems, and MO 418260 all put the point anywhere in the plane, which is what the Lean quantifies over.
- Berry's paper, which follows Guy D19, also allows points outside the square: it discusses points on the sides and solutions with negative coordinates.
- MathWorld paraphrases the problem as "a point in a unit square". An interior-only version is not known to be equivalent, but it is not the claim the cited sources pose.

Limitation: I could not read the body of Guy's D19 (Springer paywall; archive.org search-inside and Google Books were blocked). I confirmed only the section title, from Springer's free front matter. Wikipedia cites Guy (pp. 181–185) for the plane version, and the Lean follows the explicit Wikipedia and MO statements, so this does not affect the verdict.
